Each player must use 13 cards consisting of 3 cards in the top hand, 5 cards in the middle hand, and 5 cards in the bottom hand. The bottom hand must be stronger than or equal to the middle hand, and the middle hand must be stronger than or equal to the top hand. Contents 1 Overview 2 Hand Rankings 3 Deal and Play 4 Fouling/mis-setting 5 Variation: Pineapple 6 Variation: 2-7 Lowball Middle 7 Scoring 8 Fantasyland 9 Progressive Fantasyland 10 Royalties 10.1 Front/Top 10.2 Middle (when variation: 2-7 lowball middle is NOT USED) 10.3 Middle (when variation: 2-7 lowball middle is USED) 10.4 Bottom/Back Overview Open Face Chinese Poker can be abbreviated as OFCP. The goal of the game is to achieve more points than your opponent(s) by winning more hands also known as rows and/or by collecting royalties on premium hands without fouling. Each player plays cards across three hands, the top, middle, and bottom, such that at the end there are 3 cards in the top, 5 in the middle and 5 in the bottom; 13 total in the completed hand, legal or not. The game version of BGA supports 1 to 4 players. Hand Rankings The best front hand is three aces. Straights, flushes, and straight flushes are not legal front hands. A>K>Q>J>10>9>8>7>6>5>4>3>2. For the convenience of writing, 10 will be written as T below. High card (K9652): lowest possible hand. In ties, you take the value of the highest card, then the second highest... Pair (KK652): two identical cards. In ties, you compare first the value of the pair (TT652>99AKQ) Two Pair (KK662): two pairs. In ties the highest pair wins (AA662>JJ773) 3 of a Kind (KKK52): also called triplet. three identical cards. In ties you compare this trio first Straight (K9JQT): five consecutive cards. In ties you compare the highest card (AKQJT>JT987>T9876>5432A) Flush: five cards of the same suit. In ties you compare the highest card Full House (KKK55): 3 of a kind + pair. In ties you compare the value of the trio first, then the pair (33322>222AA)(666TT>66622) 4 of a Kind (KKKK2): four identical cards. In ties you compare the 4 of a kind first (33334>2222A) Straight Flush: flush + straight. Royal Flush: Ace high Straight Flush, in other words, AKQJT in the same suit. Deal and Play One player is designated dealer and deals 5 cards to each player, one at a time face down. The player to dealer's left now sets his or her 5 cards, placing them face up on the table, assigning each card to the front, middle or back hand. The other players do the same, in turn, ending with the dealer. Once all players have set their first 5 cards, play continues clockwise, starting with the player on the dealer's left. Each player in turn draws the top card of the stock, exposes it, and adds it to one of his or her three hands. Once played, cards cannot be moved from one hand to another, and when a hand has its full complement of cards (5 in the back or middle, 3 in the front), no more can be added. When everyone has 13 cards, the hands are compared and scored. The deal moves to the left after each hand. Fouling/mis-setting At the end of each round, you check the hand requirement for all players (by default Top hand ≤ Middle hand ≤ Bottom hand). If some player(s) don’t meet them, the hand is considered fouled/mis-set and has zero hand ranking. So if no players meet them, all players will score 0 for the round. Variation: Pineapple In Pineapple OFCP, the maximum number of players is 3, and 4 players are not possible. In Pineapple OFCP, instead of one card per round per player as in Original OFCP, each player is dealt three cards per round, playing two and discarding one. [Rating: 3/10] Not a fan of Poker and this isn't a card game I would choose but it isn't the worst. If you play the Pineapple+Progressive version it does force a little more card strategy and push your luck, cards are allocated 5/ then 4 lots of 2 cards allocated out of 3, discarding 1.  There are probably a variety of point scoring/gambling payoff versions floating around.

[Rating: 3/10] Card placement game where you are trying to beat your opponent in as many lines as possible. abstract card games like these not really my type. However, the concept might be quite decent and there are various modes you can choose to play with. Not something I want to keep playing.

[Rating: 6/10] Good with the right variants (Pineapple and Progressive, I think?) to make you feel you are actually having some control over playing to your outs. A fine poker variant, just not something I'm looking for regularly.

[Rating: 7/10] [Board Game Arena] As far as bet-and-bluff-less Poker variants go, this one is pretty fun. With Pineapple it's quite strategic. Do you go for a conservative board or do you go Fantasyland-or-bust? Looking at what cards are already removed from the deck and being mindful of the odds is important, so is carefully placing your initial starting hand. In physical play I think I would find the scoring rather cumbersome, especially with more than two players. On digital, this is of course no issue.

[Rating: 8/10] One of the better head-to-head pokers (along with Counterbluff and East-West and Sitting Bull). It works well at 2 or 3.  The game is very finely tuned and the scoring is excellent.  The pineapple (draw 3, play 2, discard 1) and the normal (draw 1, play 1) are both good--but pineapple with fantasyland are really the way to go. The "2-7 lowball middle" is also good. I have mixed feelings about Fantasyland variants (Qs or higher in top row means you get all 13 cards at once at the beginning to do wish as you like).  It makes it more "poker like" in that you take big chances; but it does swing it

[Rating: 10/10] I love this game and can play it over and over, especially the Progressive Pineapple variant. The 2–7 Lowball variant ain't bad either.  I always think it will be fun to teach this, forgetting about Royalty scoring and how daunting that is for new players.
